findings.title: Generated object names are lost when writing to legacy storage in Create
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` is called with `obj` and returns `created`. When an object uses `generateName` (instead of an explicit `metadata.name`), `d.Storage.Create` generates and assigns the name on the returned `created` object, or mutates `obj` concurrently if `obj` is shared. Passing the original `obj` to `d.Legacy.Create` in a background goroutine means either `Legacy.Create` receives an object without the generated name/UID from unified storage (causing legacy and unified storage to have different identifiers or fail validation), or it races with mutations on `obj`/`created` while the caller is serializing `created` for the HTTP response. `created.DeepCopyObject()` should be passed to `d.Legacy.Create`.

findings.title: Async legacy writes use request context that is canceled as soon as handler returns
findings.body: In `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` (lines 51, 110, 135, 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because `DualWriterMode3` returns immediately after `d.Storage.<Op>` completes, the HTTP server finishes the request and cancels `ctx` right away, which will cancel the in-flight or not-yet-started `d.Legacy.<Op>` calls in the goroutine. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying `context.WithTimeoutCause` so the background legacy write is not aborted when the HTTP request finishes.

findings.title: Wrong metrics recorded in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection
findings.body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record against the wrong store or with the wrong label:
- Line 45 (`Create`): when `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 106 (`Delete`): `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` as the `kind` parameter (causing high-cardinality metric labels) instead of `options.Kind`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): inside the async legacy goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Delete attaches un-enriched logger to context
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 passes `d.Log` instead of `log` to `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, losing those structured log fields in downstream calls.

findings.title: Shared testify mock.Mock in tests races with async legacy goroutines
findings.body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share a single `&mock.Mock{}` instance, and `Delete`/`DeleteCollection` do not even set up expectations on `Legacy`. Because `DualWriterMode3` invokes `d.Legacy.<Op>` in a background goroutine without synchronization, the goroutine accesses `m.Called(...)` concurrently with subsequent test assertions or after the test finishes, causing data races under `go test -race` and panics when `Delete`/`DeleteCollection` goroutines hit unexpected `Legacy` mock calls.
